claim: On 2025-12-02 Amazon S3 raised the maximum size of an object from 5 TB to 50 TB. Objects that large must be uploaded with the Multipart Upload API, and because a single GET request is limited to 5 TB, they are downloaded with concurrent GetObject requests. The largest object that a single PUT can upload is still 5 GB.
question: When did the maximum S3 object size change, from what to what, and what upload and download limits still apply?

qualifiers.condition: objects above 5 GB need multipart upload

evidence.quote: | [Large object support](#WhatsNew) | Amazon S3 has increased the maximum size of an object you can store in an S3 bucket from 5 TB to 50 TB. For uploading these larger objects, you must implement the Multipart Upload REST API to upload objects in parts, and when downloading these objects, use concurrent `GetObject` requests, as single GET requests are limited to 5 TB. For more information, see [Uploading objects](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/upload-objects.html) and [Downloading objects](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/download-objects.html). | December 2, 2025 |
The largest object that can be uploaded in a single PUT is 5 GB.

note: d158. Older questions and notes assume a 5 TB maximum object size. Current-truth fact: s3-object-max-size.

claim: On 2024-11-14 Amazon S3 raised the default bucket quota from 100 to 10,000 per AWS account, and any customer can request a quota increase up to 1 million buckets.
question: What is the default number of general purpose buckets per account, what was it before November 2024, and how high can it be raised?

qualifiers.scope: general purpose buckets per AWS account

evidence.quote: By default, you can create up to 10,000 general purpose buckets per AWS account.
Amazon S3 has increased the default bucket quota from 100 to 10,000 per AWS account.
Additionally, any customer can request a quota increase up to 1 million buckets.

note: d159. Older questions assume 100 buckets per account. Current-truth fact: s3-bucket-quota-default.

claim: On 2024-09-30 Amazon S3 began automatically approving bucket quota increases up to 1,000 buckets.
question: What did S3 change about bucket quota increase requests in September 2024?

qualifiers.condition: superseded in practice by the 10,000 default of 2024-11-14

evidence.quote: | [Amazon S3 now automatically approves bucket quota increases up to 1,000 buckets](#WhatsNew) | Amazon S3 now automatically approves bucket quota increases up to 1,000 buckets. To view your bucket utilization or request an increase, visit the [Service Quotas console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/home/services/s3/quotas/). | September 30, 2024 |

note: d159. Intermediate step only; six weeks later the default itself became 10,000. Do not teach as current.

claim: Since 2023-01-05 all new object uploads to Amazon S3 are automatically encrypted at no additional cost; SSE-S3 is applied to all new buckets and to any existing bucket that did not already have default encryption configured.
question: Since when does S3 encrypt every new object automatically, and with which method?

values.spoken: S3 managed keys, S S E S three

qualifiers.scope: every new object upload, all buckets
qualifiers.condition: existing buckets with SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS configured kept their setting

evidence.quote: Starting January 5, 2023, all new object uploads to Amazon S3 are automatically encrypted at no additional cost and with no impact on performance.
SSE-S3, which uses 256-bit Advanced Encryption Standard (AES-256), is automatically applied to all new buckets and to any existing S3 bucket that doesn't already have default encryption configured.

note: d107. Older questions offer 'turn on default encryption' as the answer to 'make sure new objects are encrypted at rest'; it is now automatic. No verbatim old-value row, so `changed` is empty.

claim: SSE-S3 is the base level of encryption for every new object uploaded to a bucket, and you can no longer disable encryption for new object uploads.
question: Can encryption be turned off for new objects written to an S3 bucket?

values.spoken: you can no longer disable encryption

evidence.quote: SSE-S3 is the new base level of encryption that's applied to all the new objects being uploaded to your bucket.
You can no longer disable encryption for new object uploads.

claim: Automatic encryption applies only to new uploads: objects already stored unencrypted in an existing bucket are not encrypted automatically, and to encrypt them you can use S3 Batch Operations to create encrypted copies.
question: Did the January 2023 default encryption change encrypt objects that were already stored, and how do you encrypt them?

values.spoken: existing objects are not encrypted automatically

values.display: S3 Batch Operations to create encrypted copies

qualifiers.scope: objects stored before default encryption applied

evidence.quote: Objects that are already in an existing unencrypted bucket won't be automatically encrypted.
To encrypt existing objects, you can use S3 Batch Operations to create encrypted copies of your objects.

note: d107. UpdateObjectEncryption (2026-01) changes the type of objects that are already encrypted; it does not support unencrypted objects, so copies remain the path for those.

claim: Since 2023-04-27 Amazon S3 automatically enables S3 Block Public Access and disables ACLs for all new buckets in all AWS Regions.
question: Since when are Block Public Access on and ACLs off by default for new S3 buckets?

values.display: Block Public Access turned on by default
values.spoken: Block Public Access is on by default

qualifiers.condition: settings can be changed after creation

evidence.quote: | [Amazon S3 enables S3 Block Public Access and disables S3 access control lists (ACLs) for all new buckets.](#WhatsNew) | Amazon S3 now automatically enables S3 Block Public Access and disables S3 access control lists (ACLs) for all new S3 buckets in all AWS Regions. For more information, see [Blocking public access to your Amazon S3 storage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-control-block-public-access.html) and [Controlling ownership of objects and disabling ACLs for your bucket](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/about-object-ownership.html). | April 27, 2023 |
All new buckets have Block Public Access turned on by default.
For newly created buckets, ACLs are disabled by default.

note: d086, d163. Older material says new buckets accept ACLs and must have Block Public Access turned on by hand. Current-truth facts: s3-block-public-access-default-on, s3-object-ownership-default-bucket-owner-enforced.

claim: On 2025-11-26 S3 Block Public Access added organization-level enforcement through AWS Organizations: a policy attached at the root or at an organizational unit propagates to all accounts in that scope, and new member accounts inherit it automatically.
question: Since when can Block Public Access be enforced for a whole AWS organization, and how does the policy reach accounts?

qualifiers.scope: per organization, root or OU or selected accounts

evidence.quote: When you attach the policy at the root or Organizational Unit (OU)-level of your organization, it propagates to all sub-accounts within that scope, and new member accounts automatically inherit the policy.
You can manage Block Public Access settings at multiple levels: organization level (using AWS Organizations), account level, and bucket and access point level.

note: d086. GA before 2026-07-15, so examinable. Older answers use an SCP that denies s3:PutAccountPublicAccessBlock plus account-level settings.

claim: Organization-level Block Public Access policies propagate automatically to the selected member accounts and override account-level settings. At the organization level all four settings are applied together as one policy; you cannot select individual settings.
question: How do organization-level Block Public Access policies interact with account settings, and can single settings be chosen at that level?

values.display: all four settings are applied together

evidence.quote: When you apply organization-level block public access policies, they automatically propagate to selected member accounts and override account-level settings.
At the organization level, all four settings are applied together as a unified policy - you cannot select individual settings granularly.

claim: Account-level Block Public Access settings inherit organization-level policies, and S3 applies the most restrictive of the bucket-level and effective account-level settings, so a bucket with Block Public Access turned off is still protected when the organization policy is on.
question: If an organization Block Public Access policy is on but one bucket has Block Public Access turned off, is that bucket protected?

qualifiers.scope: bucket, account and organization Block Public Access

evidence.quote: Account-level settings automatically inherit organization-level policies when present, and S3 takes the most restrictive policy between bucket-level and effective account-level settings.

For example, if your organization has a Block Public Access policy enabled, but a specific bucket has Block Public Access disabled at the bucket level, the bucket will still be protected because S3 applies the more restrictive organization/account-level settings.

claim: On 2025-11-19 Amazon S3 added a bucket-level default encryption setting that enforces SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS for all write requests to a bucket; with the PutBucketEncryption API you can disable SSE-C on specific buckets.
question: What bucket setting did S3 add in November 2025 to control which encryption types writers may use?

evidence.quote: Amazon S3 now supports a new default encryption configuration setting to enforce Amazon S3 managed server-side encryption (SSE-S3) or server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) for all write requests to your buckets.
Using the PutBucketEncryption API, you can disable server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C) on specific buckets or in your AWS CloudFormation templates.

note: d167. This is the setting; the April 2026 rollout (s3-change-sse-c-disabled-default-2026-04) turned it on by default. Both concern SSE-C.

claim: In April 2026 Amazon S3 deployed a default that disables SSE-C for new write requests on all new general purpose buckets, and on existing buckets in accounts that had no SSE-C encrypted objects. Applications that need SSE-C must enable it with the PutBucketEncryption API after creating the bucket. New buckets in Middle East (Bahrain) and Middle East (UAE) are excepted.
question: Is SSE-C allowed by default on a new S3 bucket today, since when, and how do you allow it?

values.display: SSE-C encryption disabled for all new write requests
values.spoken: SSE-C is off for new writes

qualifiers.condition: existing buckets in accounts with SSE-C objects were not changed; Middle East (Bahrain) and Middle East (UAE) excepted

evidence.quote: In April 2026, Amazon S3 deployed an update so all new general purpose buckets have SSE-C encryption disabled for all new write requests.
For existing buckets in AWS accounts with no SSE-C encrypted objects, Amazon S3 also disabled SSE-C for all new write requests.

With this change, applications that need SSE-C encryption must deliberately enable SSE-C by using the [PutBucketEncryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_PutBucketEncryption.html) API operation after creating a new bucket.
All newly created buckets in all AWS Regions except Middle East (Bahrain) and Middle East (UAE) will have SSE-C disabled by default.

note: d112, d167. GA before 2026-07-15, so examinable. Older questions treat SSE-C as available on every bucket. Current-truth fact: s3-sse-c-disabled-by-default-2026-04.

claim: On 2026-01-29 Amazon S3 added the UpdateObjectEncryption API, which changes the server-side encryption type of encrypted objects without any data movement, for example from SSE-S3 to SSE-KMS; with S3 Batch Operations it can standardize the encryption type of entire buckets while keeping object properties and Lifecycle eligibility.
question: Can the encryption type of existing S3 objects be changed in place, and since when?

qualifiers.scope: encrypted objects in general purpose buckets

evidence.quote: You can now change the server-side encryption type of encrypted objects in Amazon S3 without any data movement.

With UpdateObjectEncryption, customers can now change the encryption type of existing encrypted objects to move from Amazon S3 managed server-side encryption (SSE-S3) to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
With S3 Batch Operations, you can use UpdateObjectEncryption at scale to standardize the encryption type on entire buckets of objects while preserving object properties and S3 Lifecycle eligibility.

note: d117. GA before 2026-07-15, so examinable. Older answers: copy the objects onto themselves (CopyObject or Batch Operations Copy) with the new encryption settings.

claim: UpdateObjectEncryption does not support objects that are unencrypted or encrypted with DSSE-KMS or SSE-C, and you cannot specify SSE-S3 as the new type. It fails on any object that has an Object Lock retention mode or legal hold.
question: Which objects can the UpdateObjectEncryption operation not change?

values.display: doesn't support objects that are unencrypted
values.spoken: not for unencrypted, DSSE-KMS or SSE-C objects

evidence.quote: The `UpdateObjectEncryption` operation doesn't support objects that are unencrypted or objects that are encrypted with either dual-layer server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (DSSE-KMS) or customer-provided encryption keys (SSE-C).
Additionally, you cannot specify SSE-S3 encryption type `UpdateObjectEncryption` request.
The `UpdateObjectEncryption` operation fails on any object that has an S3 Object Lock retention mode or legal hold applied to it.

claim: A single Batch Operations UpdateObjectEncryption job can support a manifest with up to 20 billion objects, and the operation can also change the customer managed KMS key used to encrypt the data.
question: How many objects can one Batch Operations UpdateObjectEncryption job cover, and can it switch to another KMS key?

evidence.quote: A single `UpdateObjectEncryption` operation job can support a manifest with up to 20 billion objects.
You can also use the `UpdateObjectEncryption` operation to change the customer-managed KMS key used to encrypt your data so that you can comply with custom key-rotation standards.
